about.text: Cancoillotte or cancoyotte is a runny French cheese made from metton cheese, and produced principally in Franche-Comté, but also Lorraine and Luxembourg, where it is also called Kachkéis or Kochkäse in German. It is a typical cheese in Franc-Comtois gastronomy. It is eaten all year around, served cold or hot.

how.text: Cancoillotte starts from metton, a skim-milk curd pressed and then ripened into hard, yellowish grains; melting it at about 90 °C with water and salt turns it into a runny, low-fat spread whose texture depends on how much water is added.
